title: x *. -1. on a NaN gives a sign bit that differs from bytecode
summary: Simplify rewrites `x *. 1.` and `x /. 1.` to `x`, and `x *. -1.` and `x /. -1.` to a negation. For a NaN the result differs from what the machine computes: `Float.sign_bit (nan *. -1.)` is true in native code and false in bytecode and at `-Oclassic`; the same for `float32`, and a signalling NaN times 1. stays signalling.
cause: `middle_end/flambda2/simplify/simplify_binary_primitive.ml`: the identities are applied under a comment that says they keep the bit pattern.
